summary: Cleveland NF lookout built by the CCC in 1935; burned in 1986, struck by a Marine helicopter in 1988; only a concrete foundation remains.

facts.design: Steel K-brace tower with a wood cab (1935); the 1965 replacement had a steel cab
facts.status_note: Tower struck by a Marine helicopter in 1988 and removed; only a concrete foundation remains

access.note: Wikipedia says the site is still accessible via trail (Margarita Road/Truck Trail); no tower remains

visit.trail_note: Reached via trail (Margarita Road/Truck Trail), per Wikipedia; there is no tower to climb

events.note: CCC built the original tower: steel K-brace frame with a wood cab
A lookout named Charlton on Santa Margarita Peak, per a California Ranger item dated October 14, 1938
Replaced by a Forest Service standard CL-104 series lookout with a steel cab
August 23, 1969 fire in Devil's Canyon surrounded the tower; the garage burned, the tower did not
Wildfire burned over the 1965 tower and cabin
March 2, 1988: a Marine CH-46E helicopter collided with the tower; Wikipedia and the register call it destroyed
Tower heavily damaged in the collision and had to be removed
Former Fire Lookout Sites Register, US 517, CA 3; nominated by Brad Eells

corrections.why: Wikipedia's infobox coordinates (33.26665 N, 117.23 W) lie about 4 km from the record's point; the record's point comes from Wikidata. Medium confidence, needs a human check

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Wikipedia's 3,087 ft is labelled as the highest point; the register's 2,502 ft is given for the tower site. The story reports both and does not pick one.
Wikipedia and the register say the tower was destroyed in the March 1988 collision; the Forest Lookouts page says it was heavily damaged and had to be removed. All three agree no tower stands now.

notes_for_editor: Built, 1965 replacement, 1969 fire, 1986 burn and 1988 collision are corroborated by two or three sources. The current condition (foundation only) and the trail access rest on Wikipedia alone. 'Public' access is inferred from Wikipedia's 'still accessible via trail'; no source found on closures or trail conditions. The register's coordinates (33 deg 26.665 min N, 117 deg 23.000 min W) are more than 20 km from Wikipedia's point; they look like 33.26665 / -117.23 mistyped in degree-minute form, so the map point needs checking. The story does not use them. Elevation sources disagree (see resolved_conflicts). Not visited; no photos added.
